E1.1.1.q: A clothes shop starts selling through its own website, taking payment online and posting orders to customers. Which online service is this?
E1.1.1.why: Online retail is buying and selling goods online, with ordering, payment and delivery handled digitally.

E1.1.1.q: Which is a DISADVANTAGE of online retail for customers?
options: They can't see or try products before buying
They must travel to a shop
E1.1.1.why: Online shopping is convenient, but you can't handle goods and returns take effort.

E1.1.2.q: A customer pays bills, moves money between accounts and checks their balance on a phone app without visiting a branch. What is this?
E1.1.2.why: Banking, insurance and payments done online are online financial services.

E1.1.3.q: A student completes a certified coding course through video lessons and online quizzes at home. Which online service is this?
E1.1.3.why: Courses and qualifications delivered over the internet are online education.

E1.1.4.q: A story spreads on social media within minutes, before it has been fact-checked. Which online service, and which risk, does this show?
E1.1.4.why: Online news is instant, but unchecked stories can spread misinformation.

E1.1.5.q: A family stops buying DVDs and streams films on demand for a monthly fee instead. Which online service is this?
E1.1.5.why: Music, films, TV and games delivered on demand count as online entertainment.

E1.1.6.q: A patient checks which appointment slots are free at their GP and reserves one instantly through an app. What system is this?
E1.1.6.why: Booking systems let customers check availability and reserve in real time.

E1.2.1.q: A supermarket records every purchase: the items, time, amount and payment method. What kind of data is this?
E1.2.1.why: Transactional data is recorded each time a customer interacts with an organisation.

E1.2.2.q: After you look at trainers on one website, adverts for those trainers follow you around other sites. What is this?
E1.2.2.why: Targeted marketing uses data about your behaviour to show personalised adverts.

E1.2.3.q: Five students edit the same Google Doc at the same time from different homes. What does this show?
E1.2.3.why: Collaborative working tools let people work on the same files at once from anywhere.

E1.2.4.q: An accountant works from home three days a week using a VPN, cloud apps and video calls. What is this?
E1.2.4.why: Remote working means working away from the office with tools such as VPNs and video calls.

E1.2.4.q: Which is a DRAWBACK of remote working for an organisation?
options: Harder to keep data secure on home networks
Fewer people can apply for jobs
E1.2.4.why: Home networks and devices are harder to control, which raises security risks.

E2.1.1.q: A café wants to know what its own customers think of its new menu, so it hands out a short survey. What kind of data will this collect?
E2.1.1.why: Primary data is collected first-hand for a specific current purpose.

E2.1.2.q: A business planning a new shop uses government census figures about the local population. What kind of data is this?
E2.1.2.why: Secondary data already exists and was collected by someone else for another purpose.

E2.2.q: A student finds a surprising statistic on one website. What is the best way to check it is reliable?
options: Check it against several reputable sources
Use it because it is online
Check how many likes it has
Ask a friend if it sounds right
E2.2.why: Cross-checking against trusted, up-to-date sources is how you make sure information is reliable.

E2.3.1.q: An online shop emails structured questions to 5,000 customers after purchase to get measurable satisfaction scores. Which method is this?
E2.3.1.why: Surveys reach many people with structured questions and produce measurable data.

E2.3.2.q: Shoppers are handed a printed form with the same fixed set of written questions to fill in. Which method is this?
E2.3.2.why: A questionnaire is a fixed set of written questions on paper or online.

E2.3.3.q: An app developer invites eight potential users to try a prototype and discuss it together, led by a facilitator. Which method is this?
E2.3.3.why: A focus group is a small group discussing a topic in depth, led by a facilitator.

E2.3.4.q: A researcher wants detailed views and follow-up answers from one customer at a time. Which method is best?
E2.3.4.why: Interviews are one-to-one and allow detailed answers and follow-up questions.

E2.4.q: A hospital gives a patient the wrong drug because their allergy was recorded incorrectly. What does this show?
options: Why surveys are better than interviews
E2.4.why: Inaccurate data leads to bad decisions, harm and legal problems.

E2.5.1.q: A sign-up form asks you to type your new password twice to confirm it. Which accuracy method is this?
E2.5.1.why: Verification checks data was copied or entered correctly, e.g. by entering it twice.

E2.5.2.q: An online form refuses to accept an age of 200 and says 'Please enter an age between 16 and 100'. Which accuracy method is this?
E2.5.2.why: Validation automatically checks data is sensible and follows rules before accepting it.

E2.5.2.q: A form passes validation but the customer has typed their house number as 12 instead of 21. Why wasn't this caught?
options: Validation only checks data is sensible, not that it is correct
E2.5.2.why: 12 is a sensible value, so validation accepts it. Only verification can catch a correct-looking mistake.

E2.6.1.q: A delivery driver has to enter details on a form with no training, so it uses clear labels and a simple layout. Which characteristic is this?
E2.6.1.why: Ease of use is how easily users can find their way around and enter data without training.

E2.6.2.q: A council form supports screen readers and high-contrast text, and every field can be used with the keyboard alone. Which characteristic is this?
E2.6.2.why: Accessibility means people with disabilities can use the interface.

E2.6.3.q: Instead of a free-text box, a form gives a drop-down list of UK counties so users can't misspell them. Which characteristic is this?
E2.6.3.why: Error reduction designs stop users entering wrong data in the first place.

E2.6.4.q: Users can't finish an online claim because the form has no way to upload a photo of the receipt. Which characteristic is missing?
E2.6.4.why: Functionality is whether the interface has every feature users need to complete their tasks.

E2.6.5.q: A ticket booking form freezes when thousands of fans try to buy at once. Which characteristic is poor?
E2.6.5.why: Performance is how quickly the interface responds, including at busy times.

E2.6.6.q: A survey form looks fine on a laptop but its buttons are cut off on phones. Which characteristic has failed?
E2.6.6.why: Compatibility is whether the interface works on all devices, browsers and screen sizes.
